verdict.rationale: Svelte's first-party docs show the built-in `$state` rune creating reactive state. `.svelte.js`/`.svelte.ts` modules can use runes for "sharing reactive state across your app", and `$state` works in class fields, so global state needs no third-party library. A hands-on community report independently confirms that the built-in Stores and Context system work well for sharing state. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the stores/context APIs and caveats for global state (e.g. SSR state isolation).

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage global application state using built-in primitives without adding a third-party library

citations.quote: The `$state` rune allows you to create _reactive state_, which means that your UI _reacts_ when it changes.
These behave like any other `.js` or `.ts` module, except that you can use runes. This is useful for creating reusable reactive logic, or sharing reactive state across your app
Use `$state` in class fields for reactive properties.
Svelte Stores and the Context system are great for sharing state
